questions.prompt: In Anthropic's three build paths, which one hands the most work to Anthropic?

options.explanation: That path gives you the most control: you write the agent loop and run your own tools and infrastructure.
The SDK sits in between. It provides the loop, but in a process you operate.
Right. Anthropic hosts the agent loop, tool execution and runtime.

questions.prompt: OpenAI's agents guide rates the integration effort of each option. Which one does it rate high?

options.text: The Responses API, where you call models directly or build from scratch.
options.explanation: Right. More control comes with more work.

options.text: The Agents API, where OpenAI manages the agent and saves its progress.
options.explanation: The guide rates this one low, because OpenAI runs the agent for you.

options.text: The Agents SDK, which runs inside your own application.
options.explanation: The guide rates the SDK medium, between the other two.

questions.prompt: Why does Anthropic's "Building effective agents" post suggest care with frameworks?

options.text: Frameworks are not allowed in production systems.
options.explanation: The post doesn't forbid them. It says they help you get started, but you should understand what they do.

options.text: They can hide the underlying prompts and responses, making problems harder to debug.
options.explanation: Right. The post also says they can tempt teams to add complexity a simpler setup wouldn't need.

options.text: Frameworks always cost more money than calling the model API directly.
options.explanation: The post makes no claim about price. Its concern is hidden behaviour and extra complexity.
